questions.question: How can you lower your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Ride in parts of your lane where others can't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to catch any problems. Small mechanical issues can be dangerous on a motorcycle, more so than on a car.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other vehicles and helps them see you. It keeps you away from wind gusts, blind spots, and hazards on the road. It also stops other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They don't matter much since motorcycles are small.
They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Don't use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are more complex than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are at higher risk. Always use turn signals to alert others to your plans. Use them every time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Why is riding alongside a car dangerous?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only an issue when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the driver's blind spot, and the car blocks your escape path.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap.
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing while riding. This includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: During your pre-ride check, inspect your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: When does Massachusetts law require motorcycle headlights?

options.text: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise. It is safest to use headlights whenever you ride.

questions.question: What should you do if you can't avoid hitting an object or uneven surface?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must hit an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down, keep the motorcycle upright, and rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight to be more visible at intersections. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move out of danger if needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver go slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen only in areas where it is safe and legal to pass.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: You can be more visible by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check everything except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals. Paint damage does not affect safe riding.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
Your body is usually not affected.
Your body is affected, but only for a short time.
Your body is affected, but coffee can eliminate it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can harm your riding skills. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When riding over bumps or potholes, rise off your seat so:

options.text: You can jump off if needed.
Your legs can absorb the impact.
You can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off the seat lets your joints absorb some of the shock. This keeps the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another durable material for proper protection.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like most food and drinks. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker right away.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly once it is in your system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker right away.
questions.explanation: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain in minutes. The body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show traffic rules, like speed limits, are rectangular and white with black letters or symbols. Drivers must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather when riding. It protects you in a crash. Leather jackets are designed to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: Wearing a helmet is:

options.text: Required for both riders and passengers.
Required only for riders under age 21.
Optional for both riders and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for both riders and passengers.
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires all motorcycle riders and passengers to wear a helmet. A DOT-approved helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your body even at this rate. Your abilities and judgment may still be impaired.
